title: Sail through the Hole in the Rock at Piercy Island
description: Motukokako, a sea-carved arch at the tip of Cape Brett that boats pass through when the swell allows. Dolphins are common on the run out.

title: Stand on the Treaty grounds at Waitangi
description: Where the Treaty was signed in 1840 - the founding document of New Zealand, and still the country's most argued-over. The guided tour is worth it.

title: Walk the Cape Brett Track to the lighthouse
description: 16km each way along a knife-edge peninsula to a hut beside the lighthouse. Eight hours in, and the only easy way out is by boat.

title: Kayak to the Haruru Falls through the mangroves
description: A horseshoe waterfall reached by paddling up the Waitangi River - go on an incoming tide and let the water do the work.

title: Wander the old whaling port of Russell
description: Once called the hell hole of the Pacific, now the quietest place in the bay - Christ Church still carries musket holes from 1845.

title: Watch two oceans collide at Cape Reinga
description: Te Rerenga Wairua, where Maori believe spirits depart - and where the Tasman Sea visibly meets the Pacific in a line of standing waves.

title: Sandboard the Te Paki dunes
description: Giant dunes at the top of Ninety Mile Beach that you climb on foot and come down on a boogie board, considerably faster than expected.

title: Drive the length of Ninety Mile Beach
description: A gazetted highway on sand, actually about 88km. Rental agreements almost always forbid it - the safe way is the bus that does it daily.

title: Swim at Matai Bay on the Karikari Peninsula
description: Twin white-sand coves in a DOC reserve, sheltered from almost every wind direction, with a campground behind the dunes.

title: Stand beneath Tane Mahuta in Waipoua Forest
description: The largest living kauri, roughly 51m and possibly 2,000 years old. Scrub your boots at the station - kauri dieback is spread by soil on footwear.

title: Sandboard the Hokianga dunes at Opononi
description: A boat drops you at the giant dunes across the harbour mouth, and you slide back down toward the water. Opononi is where Opo the dolphin lived in 1955.

title: Dive the Poor Knights Islands
description: Cousteau rated this among the world's top dives - a subtropical current brings species found nowhere else this far south, into drowned volcanic caves.

title: Walk to the top of Whangarei Falls
description: A 26m curtain over a basalt lip, with a loop track that puts you at the top, the bottom and behind the spray in about forty minutes.

title: Snorkel the marine reserve at Goat Island
description: New Zealand's first marine reserve, protected since 1975 - snapper come close enough to touch because nobody has fished them in fifty years.

title: Surf the point at Sandy Bay, Tutukaka
description: The most consistent beach break on the Tutukaka Coast, with a long right-hander off the northern rocks when a swell is running.

title: Walk the Mangawhai Cliffs clifftop loop
description: Up onto the cliffs and back along the beach - the return leg only works at low tide, so check the table before you start.

title: Climb the crater rim of Rangitoto
description: Auckland's youngest volcano, erupted about 600 years ago and visible from everywhere in the city. A scoria climb through the largest pohutukawa forest on earth.

title: Hear the dawn chorus on Tiritiri Matangi
description: A predator-free island replanted by volunteers, now holding takahe, kokako and saddleback. Stay the night and the dawn chorus is genuinely startling.

title: Cycle between the vineyards on Waiheke Island
description: Forty minutes by ferry from downtown Auckland to an island of Bordeaux-style reds, olive groves and beaches. Hilly - take the e-bike.

title: Walk the black sand at Piha
description: Iron sand that gets painfully hot, a serious rip, and Lion Rock in the middle of it. Swim between the flags - this beach earns its reputation.

title: Watch the gannet colony at Muriwai
description: Around 1,200 pairs of takapu nesting on a headland stack, close enough that you can watch a chick being fed from the viewing platform.

title: Find the waterfall at Karekare
description: The beach from The Piano, and a short walk inland to a fall dropping into a swimming hole. Check current kauri dieback track closures before going.

title: Jump off the Sky Tower
description: A 192m base-wire jump off the tallest building in the Southern Hemisphere, at 85km/h, landing on a target in the plaza below.

title: Climb Maungawhau for the volcanic field view
description: Mount Eden, the highest of Auckland's 53 volcanoes, with a 50m crater on top. Walking into the crater is prohibited - it is a sacred site.

title: See the Maori court at Auckland Museum
description: Holds Hotunui, a carved meeting house from 1878, and Te Toki a Tapiri, the last great Maori war canoe - 25m from a single totara.

title: Take the ferry to Devonport and walk up North Head
description: Twelve minutes across the harbour to a Victorian village, then up a headland honeycombed with tunnels and gun emplacements from the 1880s Russian scare.

title: Eat your way through the Auckland Fish Market
description: A working auction floor with eating houses built around it - the snapper and the Bluff oysters in season are the reason to come.

title: Have a pint at the Green Dragon in Hobbiton
description: The only permanent set left standing from the films - 44 hobbit holes on a working sheep farm, rebuilt in wood and plaster to last.

title: Float under the glowworms in the Waitomo Caves
description: A boat drifts in silence beneath a ceiling of Arachnocampa luminosa found nowhere else on earth. The guides ask for quiet, and it matters.

title: Black-water raft through the Ruakuri cave system
description: Abseil in, then float an underground river on an inner tube through the dark with glowworms overhead. Cold, wet and genuinely exhilarating.

title: Walk the Marokopa Falls track
description: A 36m fall through a limestone gorge on the road west of Waitomo, with the Mangapohue natural bridge and Piripiri Cave on the same drive.

title: Learn to surf the point break at Manu Bay
description: One of the longest and most reliable left-hand point breaks in the world, and the wave that made Raglan famous through The Endless Summer.

title: Walk in behind Bridal Veil Falls
description: Waireinga drops 55m off a basalt lip in a single clean column, with viewing platforms at the top, halfway down and at the plunge pool.

title: Dig your own hot pool at Hot Water Beach
description: Geothermal water rises through the sand for two hours either side of low tide - bring a spade and get there early to claim a patch.

title: Walk to Cathedral Cove
description: A limestone arch joining two beaches. Cyclone Gabrielle wrecked the access track in 2023 and repairs have run for years - check DOC before you drive out.

title: Ride the Driving Creek Railway
description: A narrow-gauge line the potter Barry Brickell built by hand over 35 years to haul clay, climbing through replanted native bush to the Eyefull Tower.

title: Walk the Karangahake Gorge tunnel and tramway
description: A 1km unlit rail tunnel, swing bridges and the ruins of a gold battery, in a gorge that was one of the richest goldfields in the country.

title: Climb the Pinnacles from the Kauaeranga Valley
description: Up old kauri-logging packhorse steps to a hut, then a ladder scramble to a rock summit for sunrise over both coasts of the peninsula.

title: Walk through the themed gardens at Hamilton Gardens
description: Not a botanic collection but a set of fully enclosed period gardens - Italian Renaissance, Japanese, Indian Char Bagh, and a Tudor knot garden.

title: Watch 220,000 litres a second go through Huka Falls
description: The Waikato River squeezes from 100m wide into an 15m granite chute. The volume is the point - it is less a waterfall than a firehose.

title: Kayak to the Mine Bay Maori rock carvings
description: A 14m carving of Ngatoroirangi cut into the cliff in the late 1970s, reachable only by boat or kayak across Lake Taupo.

title: Soak in the free hot stream at Otumuheke
description: A geothermal stream runs into the cold Waikato River, so you can find whatever temperature you like where the two mix. Free, and busy for good reason.

title: Skydive over Lake Taupo
description: One of the cheapest and busiest drop zones anywhere, over a lake the size of Singapore with three volcanoes on the horizon.

title: Walk to the Tokaanu thermal pools
description: A boardwalk over mud pools and silica terraces at the southern end of the lake, with private thermal baths in the village for a few dollars.
